operator_asks_outbound_msg_chk.def: CREATE TRIGGER operator_asks_outbound_msg_chk BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF outbound_msg_id, committed_date, closed_at ON public.operator_asks FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operator_asks_outbound_msg_trg()
operator_asks_outbound_msg_chk.function_def:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.operator_asks_outbound_msg_trg()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
DECLARE
    msg_created_at timestamptz;
BEGIN
    -- Only an OPEN row is checked; a historical closed row (34 of them,
    -- predating this migration) is never touched by it, even if later
    -- UPDATEd for an unrelated reason. closed_at is in this trigger's own
    -- column list (console bus #80764 fix 2 -- the "reopen hole"): without
    -- it, reopening a closed row (closed_at set back to NULL) while it still
    -- carries an old bad link was never checked at all.
    IF NEW.closed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;

    -- Clearing both columns together is how fleet-health lifts a bad link
    -- (console bus #80736) -- nothing to check when there is no commitment.
    IF NEW.committed_date IS NULL THEN
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;

    SELECT created_at INTO msg_created_at
      FROM operator_messages
     WHERE id = NEW.outbound_msg_id AND direction = 'outbound';

    IF msg_created_at IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'operator_asks.outbound_msg_id % is not a real outbound '
            'operator_messages row -- clear committed_date + outbound_msg_id, '
            'or link the real outbound', NEW.outbound_msg_id;
    END IF;

    -- console bus #80764 fix 1: the predates check belongs HERE, not only in
    -- asks_triage.py -- the CLI is one writer, this trigger covers all of
    -- them. A message from before the ask existed cannot have committed
    -- its date.
    IF msg_created_at < NEW.created_at THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'operator_asks.outbound_msg_id % (sent %) predates this ask '
            '(created %); it cannot have committed this date -- clear committed_date '
            '+ outbound_msg_id, or link the real outbound',
            NEW.outbound_msg_id, msg_created_at, NEW.created_at;
    END IF;

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$function$

work_item_mirror_ask_trg.def: CREATE TRIGGER work_item_mirror_ask_trg AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON public.operator_asks FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION work_item_mirror_ask_trg()
work_item_mirror_ask_trg.function_def:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.work_item_mirror_ask_trg()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
BEGIN
    -- The mirror must NEVER be able to block the system of record (orch-console review,
    -- bus #73195): an exception in here degrades to "work_item missing/stale for this one
    -- row, surfaced loudly", never an aborted operator_asks write. The 2026-10-24
    -- equivalence proof is the drift backstop that catches anything skipped this way.
    BEGIN
        -- GREATEST(committed_date, chase_by): due_at is "don't flag me as
        -- abandoned before this", and either date can independently express
        -- that (op#35246, bus #81038/#81040). GREATEST ignores a NULL
        -- argument unless both are NULL.
        PERFORM work_item_mirror('ask', 'operator_asks', NEW.id,
            work_item_derive_ask(NEW.id, NEW.ask, NEW.triage_state, NEW.closed_at,
                                  NEW.delegated_to, GREATEST(NEW.committed_date, NEW.chase_by),
                                  NEW.triaged_by),
            'trigger:operator_asks');
    EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'work_item mirror failed for operator_asks id=%: %', NEW.id, SQLERRM;
    END;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$function$
